beats.text: Every inch you're taller is worth money. About seven hundred and eighty-nine dollars a year.
Researchers followed about eighty-five hundred people from their teens into their careers, in the US and the UK.
Even after accounting for gender, age and weight, taller people earned more.
Six feet versus five foot five? That's about a hundred and sixty-six thousand dollars over a thirty-year career.
One explanation: height makes people seem more confident, and they get treated that way.
Unfair? Absolutely. But now you know it's there.

sources: Judge & Cable (2004). The effect of physical height on workplace success and income. Journal of Applied Psychology 89(3). Four longitudinal datasets (~8,500 people, US & UK) + meta-analysis of 45 studies; each inch ~ $789/year; 6' vs 5'5" ~ $166,000 over 30 years, controlling for gender, age, weight; self-esteem/social esteem explanation. Via APA Monitor 2004.
